title: Profiteroles
subtitle: choux pastry puffs filled with cream and drenched in chocolate sauce
excerpt: Profiteroles are made from choux pastry -- a cooked dough that puffs dramatically in the oven and collapses into a crisp, hollow shell. Fill with whipped cream and pour warm chocolate sauce over the top. They should be assembled just before eating.
sourceNotes: A French patisserie classic. Profiteroles became a fixture on British restaurant menus in the 1970s and remain popular.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unfilled shells. Refresh in a hot oven for 5 minutes before filling.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the shells a day ahead and store in an airtight tin. Fill and sauce on the day.
recipe.temperatureNote: Conventional oven -- do not open the door during baking

content.text: The choux dough must be cooked on the hob before the eggs go in. Beat the eggs in one at a time until the dough is shiny and drops reluctantly from a spoon. Do not open the oven during baking -- the steam inside is what makes the shells puff. Make a small hole in each shell as soon as they come out of the oven to let steam escape.

items.prepNote: for the filling -- whip to soft peaks
use 200g dark chocolate (70%) for the sauce

content.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Bring the water, milk, and butter to a rolling boil in a saucepan. Add the sifted flour and salt all at once. Beat vigorously with a wooden spoon until the dough pulls away from the sides and forms a ball. Cook over low heat for 1 more minute, stirring. Remove from heat.
Leave to cool for 5 minutes. Beat in the eggs a little at a time, mixing vigorously between each addition. The dough should be smooth and glossy and drop reluctantly from the spoon when shaken.

Pipe or spoon 24 small mounds (about 3cm diameter) onto lined baking sheets. Wet your finger and press down any peaks. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until puffed, golden, and crisp. Do not open the oven door.
Pierce each shell with a skewer immediately to release steam. Leave to cool.

Make the chocolate sauce: melt the dark chocolate with 100ml double cream and 50ml water in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth. Split the shells and fill with whipped cream. Pour the warm sauce over to serve.

items.symptom: Choux puffs collapse when out of the oven
items.cause: Under-baked, or steam was not released.
items.fix: Bake until deeply golden -- pale shells will always collapse. Pierce immediately when out of the oven.

items.symptom: Dough is too stiff to pipe
items.fix: Continue adding egg a tablespoon at a time and beating well. The dough is ready when it drops slowly from a wooden spoon.

content.text: Profiteroles are French patisserie. They arrived on British menus in the postwar years and were a staple of the 1970s dinner party. They look impressive but the technique is straightforward. The chocolate sauce is the best part -- make more than you think you need.
